summary: Retained FidelityManager PR #385 documents maxRegisteredEntities as a hard bounded-state budget but validates only positive finite integer shape. Caller configuration can therefore set an impractically enormous finite integer and effectively remove the project-owned registration envelope, leaving _states bounded only by process memory rather than a project maximum.
evidence: PR #385 exact head 827ce0cf63ca5f322502de883beb9f43581c69f2 validateConfig() accepts maxRegisteredEntities when it is a number >= 1, finite, and math.floor(value) == value; it has no project-owned upper ceiling

FidelityManager.register() grows the private _states table until _metrics.registered reaches that caller-provided value, so a huge accepted configuration can bypass the intended bounded-record envelope

Docs/FIDELITY_MANAGER.md calls maxRegisteredEntities a configurable hard budget, says the registered set is bounded, and states total records are capped by configuration; QUALITY_STANDARD requires bounded caches/state and explicit performance/memory budgets

Repository PR/issue search found existing Fidelity capacity work only for malformed-scalar rejection and validation ordering (#274/#335/#385); no retained PR or open issue defines an upper registration ceiling

The current WorldEntity backfill independently treats caller-only enormous capacities as violating the same bounded-resource rule (#413), so this is consistent project hardening rather than a new feature
recommendation: Create a narrow source-only one-shot Hero-Gate lane that adds an explicit project-owned maximum registration capacity above the existing 4096 default, rejects max+1 before manager construction/policy use, and adds exact maximum/maximum+1 deterministic regressions. Preserve current F0-F4 policy, transition atomicity, identity, and Studio evidence boundaries. The ceiling should remain a defensive envelope, not a device performance claim.
